comments.content: The saved filename uses second-granularity `int(datetime.now().timestamp())`, so two concurrent uploads with the same prefix within the same second write to the same path: if request B saves between A's `file.save()` and A's `load_workbook()`, A processes B's workbook (or B's load fails after A's later handling). This behavior predates the refactor, but consolidating it here makes this helper the single point to fix it — use a unique name (e.g. `uuid.uuid4().hex`) or `tempfile.mkstemp(dir=...)` instead of the timestamp.

comments.content: `accept=".xlsx"` only filters the file-picker dialog; it does not constrain drag-and-drop, so dropping a non-.xlsx file is accepted into state and only rejected when the user submits (the pages' extension check). Now that this UI is shared, a client-side extension check in `onDrop` would fail fast in one place for both pages. If you filter silently here, make sure the user still gets feedback (e.g. an optional `onRejected` callback) rather than ignoring the drop.

comments.content: The dropzone is activated via `onClick` only, so keyboard users cannot open the file dialog (no focus target, no Enter/Space handling). Both legacy inline implementations had the same gap, but the shared component is the right place to fix it once: add `role="button"`, `tabIndex={0}` and an Enter/Space `onKeyDown` that triggers `inputRef.current?.click()`.
comments.suggestion_code:
<div
      role="button"
      tabIndex={0}
      aria-label="上传 Excel 文件"
      onKeyDown={(event) => {
        if (event.key === "Enter" || event.key === " ") {
          event.preventDefault();
          inputRef.current?.click();
        }
      }}
      className={`excel-import-dropzone ${className}${file ? " has-file" : ""}${isDragOver ? " is-dragover" : ""}`}
      onClick={(event) => {
        if (event.target !== inputRef.current) inputRef.current?.click();
      }}

comments.content: When a file is set via drag-and-drop, the hidden <input type="file"> keeps its previous value. If the user then re-picks that same file through the dialog, onChange never fires (the input value didn't change), so the click selection appears to do nothing and the stale dropped file stays selected. Since the picker and drop paths now write the same state through this shared component, clear the input's value when handling a drop so both paths stay independent. (Carried over from the legacy inline code, but this shared component is the right place to fix it once.)
